the f6-knight from the kingside.] Well played! Black's best kingside defender
must retreat and White has dangerous attacking chances.} (9. exd5 $2 exd5 {
Black is doing well. Try again and look for a better pawn move.}) *

{What strong sacrifice gives White a winning attack?} 16. Nd5 {[%wrong There's
a better move. Try again and check the hint if you're stuck.] [%hint Sacrifice
a knight to decoy the e6-pawn to a worse square.]} (16. h5 $5 {This is a
useful quiet move, but there's a sacrifice that's stronger. Try to find it.}) (
16. Ne4 $2 h6 {White is only slightly better. Try again and look for a
stronger knight move.}) (16. Rxd7 $2 Qxd7 {Black wins material and White is in
trouble. Try again and look for a stronger sacrifice.}) (16. Bh6 $2 gxh6 {
Black wins material and White is in trouble. Try again and look for a stronger
sacrifice.}) (16. Ng5 $2 Bxg5 {Black is OK after the trade on g5. Try again
and look for a powerful sacrifice.}) 16... exd5 {Qc8 would have been a better
try for Black. Now White wins back material with a devastating attack. How
should you do it?} 17. cxd5 {[%wrong Black has good chances to hold on. Try
again and look for a way to win material.] [%hint Recapture with a threat.]} (
17. e6 $5 {This is a good move, but GM Shaposhnikov chose a good capture. What
did he play?}) (17. Rxd5 $5 {This is a strong capture, but GM Shaposhnikov
captured another way. What was his idea?}) 17... Nd4 {Well played! How should
you win material?} 18. Nxd4 {[%wrong There's a stronger option. Try again and
look for a good capture.] [%hint Trade pieces instead of moving the queen.]} (
18. Rxd4 $5 {White's doing well, but there's a better capture. Try to find it.}
) (18. e6 $2 Nxe2+ {Black wins the queen with check. Try again and look for a
good capture.}) 18... cxd4 {Good idea! How can you win material?} 19. d6 {
[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and look for a strong fork.] [%hint
Fork a black queen and bishop.]} (19. e6 $5 {This is a good move, but let's
use a fork to win back the sacrificed piece. How should you do it?}) (19. Rxd4
$5 {This is a good move, but let's use a fork to win back the sacrificed piece.
How should you do it?}) 19... Bxd6 {Great work! How should you win back the
sacrificed piece?} 20. exd6 {[%wrong There's a better option. Try again and
look for a good capture.] [%hint Capture a piece to win material.] Good move!
White wins back the lost piece with a strong attack. We will revisit the game
Shaposhnikov - Sanzhaev, 2015 in the next challenge.} *

squares.} 13. h6 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try again and look for a way
to expose the black king.] [%hint Offer a trade for the key g7-pawn.]} (13. Ne3
$2 h6 {The h6-pawn prevents White from dominating the kingside dark squares.
Try again and look for a way to prevent the h7-h6 advance.}) (13. N3h2 $2 Ndxe5
{Black wins a pawn. Try again and look for a way to dominate the kingside dark
squares.}) (13. N1h2 $2 h6 {The h6-pawn prevents White from dominating the
kingside dark squares. Try again and look for a way to prevent the h7-h6
advance.}) (13. Bf4 $2 h6 {The h6-pawn prevents White from dominating the
kingside dark squares. Try again and look for a way to prevent the h7-h6
advance.}) 13... g6 {Good start! How should White begin to activate the
f1-knight?} 14. N1h2 {[%wrong There's a better move. Try to find the strongest
square for your f1-knight.] [%hint Maneuver the f1-knight to g4 without
blocking your c1-bishop.] Good choice! The knight aims for g4 and eventually
f6, which will lead to a strong attack.} (14. Bf4 $5 {This was played by GM
Anish Giri, but it's also strong to bring the f1-knight toward the g4-square.
How should you do it?}) (14. N3h2 $2 Ndxe5 {It's more active to use h2 for
another piece. How should you do it?}) (14. a3 $2 bxa3 {White is slightly
better, but there's no need to open the queenside. Try again and look for a
way to activate the f1-knight.}) (14. a4 $2 c4 {White is slightly better, but
there's no need to block the queenside. Try again and look for a way to
activate the f1-knight.}) (14. Ne3 $5 {This is OK, but there's an even better
way for this knight to reach g4 without blocking the c1-bishop. Where should
it go?}) (14. N1d2 $2 Qc7 {It's better to activate the f1-knight on the
kingside. How should you do it?}) *
